name: 1. New Contract Term
text: i. The Times and the Union agree to a new Contract (the "Contract™) for a term of six years from March 31, 1987 to March 30, 1993. The Contract shall be the present contract with the changes made by this Memorandum of Agreement.

name: 2(a). Wage Increases 1987-1988
text: (a) Effective March 31, 1987, the weekly journeyman day scale shall be increased by $43.35 a week. Pension and welfare contributions shall be made on this amount. Effective March 31, 1987, an additional §3.67 per shift from wages and after taxes (maximum of five (5) shifts) shall be contributed to the Welfare Fund. Payments retroactive to March 31, 1987 shall be made no later than thirty (30) days from the date of ratification of this Memorandum of Agreement. Effective March 31, 1988, the weekly journeyman day scale shall be increased by $35 a if FUNDO0001069 week. Payments retroactive to March 31, 1988 shall be made no later than thirty (30) days fron the date of ratification of this Memorandum of Agreement.

name: 2(b). Wage Increases 1989-1992
text: (b) The weekly journeyman day scale shall be increased by $43 a week on March 31, 1989; by '$40 a week on March 31, 1990; by $36 a week on March 31, 1991; and by $36 — a week on March 3], 1992.

name: 2(c). Cost of Living Adjustments
text: (C) Cost of living adjustments shall be made effective March 31, 1988, March 31, 1989, March 31, 1990, March 31, 1991, and March 31, 1992, pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Contract. [The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Price Index (1967 = 100) (CPI-W) for New York, New York = Northeastern New Jersey (Index) hall be used for measurement of the change.)

name: 3. Application of Contract at New or Rebuilt Facilities; Arbitration
text: 3. The Times and the Union agree that the Contract shall have full force and effect at the Edison, New Jersey by The Times within the Northeast Corridor (Maine te Northern Virginia). Because of the magnitude of the investment in new and rebuilt plants The Times is Planning and its importance to the future of the business and the security of the members of the Union, The Times and the Union are committed to the orderly, successful and efficient start-up and operation of the new and rebuilt plants. The af FUNDO0001070 Times and the Union therefore reaffirm that any dispute concerning the interpretation and application of the Contract, including any dispute concerning the interpretation and application of the Contract at anew or rebuilt facility, shall be resolved through the Contract's grievance and arbitration procedure. Without limiting the disputes to be resolved pursuant to the Contract's grievance and arbitration procedure, the parties intend to resolve all questions that may arise from innovations in methods of operation, as for example operations with palletizing equipment, by discussion and arbitration if necessary, it being understood that notwithstanding the introduction of any such new methods, the Contract will continue to protect regular situation holders against layoffs for the term of the Contract because of the introduction of automated processes. The Times agrees that all such protected regular situation holders shall be listed by name on the date of ratification and on the date of the commencement of built facility. With respect to a eee Ee i ot ate é ae at tae he & erations at any ne the commencement of operations at any new or rebuilt facility, every effort shall be made to place employees in jobs most nearly equivalent to the work peformed in current operations. It is further agreed that to the extent practicable regular situation holders engaged in advance product production at Carlstadt shall constitute the initial work force at Edison. if FUNDOO001071 | « : ok ‘ In connection with any arbitration concerning the interpretation and application of the Contract at @ new or rebuilt facility, the arbitrator shall issue his award before operations commence. Should the arbitrator fail to issue his award before operations at a new or rebuilt facility begin, operations shall commence under operating conditions established in an interim ruling by the arbitrator and shall continue thus until the arbitrator issues his award. Upon the written request of either party, the parties agree to attempt to resolve any issues under | this paragraph prior to arbitration through non-binding mediation by a mutually agreed upon mediator. The use of mediation shall not delay any arbitration proceeding on any euch issues.

text: 6. Various shop disputes are resolved as set forth in Appendix A to this Memorandum of Agreement.

name: 7. Non-Discrimination Amendment to Section 4
text: 7. The Times and the Union agree that Section 4 ~ Hiring Practices-Seniority of the 1981-84 Collective Bargaining Agreement shall be amended to include a new on, TW oe section which shall provide as follows: “There shall be no discrimination in hiring or in any other condition of employment by reason of color, race, sex, religion or national origin."

name: 8. Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance Increase
text: é. Effective upon ratification of this Memorandum of Agreement, the Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance Coverage provided for in Section 3-H.2 of the Collective Bargaining Agreement shall be increased from $60,000 to $75,000.

name: 9. Jury Service Pay
text: 9. Effective upon the ratification of this Memorandum of Agreement, Group I employees not so scheduled shall be paid for jury service based upon the number of days per week that he or she worked during the eight weeks prior to reporting for jury service. Section l3-J = Jury Service of ii FUNDO001074 the Collective Bargaining Agreement shall be amended to reflect this change.

name: 10. Revision of Section 6-D (Foreman)
text: 10. Section 6-D of the 1981-84 Collective Bargaining Agreement shall be deleted and revised as follows: "Whenever the Publisher has one or more Plants, there shall be a foreman or * assistant foreman in each plant."

name: 11. Letter Regarding Weekly Welfare Fund Contributions
text: dl. The Times will provide the Union with a letter regarding weekly contributions to the Welfare Fund, attached as Appendix € to this Memorandum of Agreement.

name: 12. Letter Regarding Section 3-P Interpretation
text: 12. The Times will provide the Union with a letter regarding The Times' interpretation of Contract Section 3-P as set forth in the 1981-84 Cellective Bargaining Agreement, attached as Appendix D to this Memorandum of Agreement.

name: 13. Letter of Understanding on Arbitrator Designations
text: 13. The Times and the Union agree to execute a letter of understanding regarding the designations of "Status Quo" and Merits Arbitrators, attached as Appendix E to this Menorandum of Agreement.

name: 14. Survival of Existing Agreements
text: 14. All letter agreements, side agreements, supplementary agreements, memoranda of agreement and | memoranda of understanding in effect on the date hereof, and all terms and conditions contained in the 1981-84 contract i FUNDO001075 booklet, shall remain in full force and effect unless modified by this Memorandum of Agreement. All dates in the Contract shall be updated to reflect this Memorandum of Agreement. If any conflict occurs between the terms of this Memorandum of Agreement and any other agreement, the terms of this Memorandum of Agreement shall prevail.

name: 15. Execution of New Contract Document
text: 15. Promptly after execution of this Memorandum of Agreement, the parties shall prepare and execute a complete new contract document (The New York Times Agreement) embodying the provisions contained in the Contract as modified to reflect and effectuate the changes agreed to herein.

name: 16. Effective Date
text: 16. This Memorandum of Agreement shall be effective immediately following Union ratification.

name: Appendix A, 1.A. Ten Additional Floor Regular Situations
text: i. Subject to there being no increase in the number of floor hires as set forth in the Collective Bargaining Agreement, it is agreed that: A. Ten additional floor regular situations (Wednesday~Saturday days at the Carlstadt plant and Sunday night at the 43d Street plant) shall be created.

name: Appendix A, 1.B. Five Additional Floor Regular Situations and Chauffeurs
text: B. Five additional floor regular situations (Wednesday-Saturday night at the Carlstadt Plant and Sunday night at the 43d Street plant) shall be created and five additional chauffeurs on dayside (4 days and Monday night).

name: Appendix A, 2. Third Recovery Car Situation
text: Ze One regular situation shall be created for the third recovery car.

name: Appendix A, 3. Jitney ("Blue Goose") Work
text: 3. The jitney ("Blue Googe") work as set forth in pages 104-5 of the 1981-4 Collective Bargaining Agreement shall be updated to reflect the names of the two employees that presently hold these job bids.

name: Appendix B, Home Delivery Copies
text: Home delivery copies shall continue to be served by having routemen deliver papers for one or more home delivery dealers, agents, or TeRoute contractors to delivery points designated by the Publisher at which the Papers will be picked up and delivered to the home delivery customers by the home delivery Gealers, agents or T-Route contractors,

name: Appendix B, West Side Direct Routes
text: The present Memorandum of Agreement on "West Side Direct Routes" entered into on November 22, 1983 shall be abolished and The Times shall have the right to reorganize these routes, provided the present number of routes in the West Side Direct operation Shall not be reduced during the term of this Agreement.

name: Appendix B, Honor Boxes and Vending Machines
text: With respect to Honor Boxes and Vending Machines, se. Appendix B-1.

name: Appendix B, Returns Handling
text: All returns, except unsold current coples on *bulldog* routes, shall be handled by the dealers' wailing to the Publisher the headsheet or other designated portion of each copy for counting and order regulation by the Publisher or its designee. Any existing physical pick-up of such copies shall continue for the duration of this Contract.

name: Appendix B-1, Honor Boxes and Vending Machines Side Letter
text: This side-letter confirms that with respect to Honor Boxes and Vending Machines The Times and the Union agree to maintain present Practices in such deliveries in The Times direct operation,

name: Appendix C, Weekly Contributions to the Welfare Fund
text: Within 30 days after ratification, contributions to the Welfare Fund (Publishers'-Newspaper and Mail Deliverers' Welfare Fund) shall be made weekly. Such payments for any payroll week shall be made available no later than ten (10) days following the end of such payroll week.

name: Appendix D, Section 3-P Interpretation of Grandfather/Grandmother
text: The Union has asked that The Times Clarify its interpretation of the terms "Grandfather" and "Grandmother" as used in Section 3-P of the Contract, polnting out that the terms have not always been interpreted and applied consistently. This will confirm that these terns mean the Grandfather or Grandmother of a Regular Situation Holder or Group I Extra or of his or her spouse at the time the grandparent dies.

name: Appendix D, No Retroactive Effect
text: This letter shall not have retroactive effect, and shall not be used or referred to in Support of any claim for leave under Section 3-P on account of a death occurring prior to the date hereof.

text: Glen Burnie/Lancaster The Times and the Union will discuss and identify the present problems concerning the transport of The Times! existing Television Magazine from Glen Burnie, Maryland to The Times's Carlstadt er Edison, New Jersey plant. name: Diversion of Wages to Vacation Pay Benefit
text: The Times agrees that on or after March 31, 1990 the Union may divert a uniform portion of each employee's wage increase to become effective then or thereafter to a vacation pay benefit.

name: No Increased Cost from Diversion; Cooperation
text: It is agreed that such diversion shall not result in any increase in cost to The Times other ‘an nominal administrative costs and that The Times will fully cooperate with the Union in developing any such alternatives and researching the financial details thereof.

name: Earnings Bonus 1. 1987 Bonus Already Paid
text: 1. It is acknowleged that The Times has already paid the Earnings Bonus for 1987 at the rate of 5.112% of the gross wages paid such employees in 1987 notwithstanding any provision to the contrary and will not seek to recalculate said bonus or to seek credit or set-off for the amounts paid, except that it is understood and agreed that no Earnings Bonus shall be paid for the retroactive wages for 1987 paid in 1988 for the general increase effective March 31, 1987.

name: Earnings Bonus 2. Bonus for 1988-1992
text: 2. _For calendar years 1988, 1989, 1990, 1991 ana 1992, the Earnings Bonus will be 3.86% of the gross wages paid the employee by The Tines Guring the applicable year.

name: Earnings Bonus 3. Bonus for January 1 - March 30, 1993
text: Je For the period January 1, 1993 through March 30, 1993, the Earnings Bonus wil} be 3.86% of the gross wages paid the employee by The Times during such pericd.

name: Earnings Bonus 4(a). Definition of Gross Wages
text: 4. (a) “Gross wages" means compensation reported as “wages, tips and other compensation" on the employee's W-2 Form for the applicable bonus period, excluding any Earnings Bonus received during that bonus period and for calendar year 1988 excluding any retroactive wages for 1987 paid in 1988 for the general increase effective March 31, 1987, The Earnings Bonus shal] be reported on a separate W-2 Form.

name: Earnings Bonus 4(b). Disability and Workers' Compensation Benefits
text: (b) However, with regard to those shifts for which an employee receives benefits under The Times Disability Plan, the employee's state disability benefit or workers' compensation benefit for such shifts shall be added to the employee's gross wages for purposes of calculating the employee's Earnings Bonus, to the extent that guch State disability and workers! compensation benefits do Not appear on the employee's W-2 Forn.

name: Earnings Bonus 5. Payment Deadline
text: 5, The Earnings Bonus shall be paid within 60 Gays after the end of the applicable bonus period.

name: Earnings Bonus 6. Continuation After March 30, 1993
text: 6. The continuation or other disposition of the Earnings Bonus after March 30, 1993 shall be Getermined by negotiations between The Times and the Union in accordg with the Contract, except that if the Parties have not agreed by March 30, 1993 on the continuation Or other disposition of the Earnings Bonus after March 30, 1993, effective March 31, 1993 the Earnings Bonus shai] cease and $25.93 at the Union's option shall be added to the weekly wage scales or allocated in the manner set forth in Paragraph 7. The Earnings Bonus due for the period January 1, 1993 through March 30, 1993 shall be paid, if not continued, within thirty (30) days after March 30, 1993,

name: Earnings Bonus 7. Union's Right to Terminate
text: 7. The Union reserves the right during the tern of the Contract, on thirty (30) days notice to The Times, to terminate these Earnings Bonus provisions and apply $25.93 to the weekly wage scales or te any fringe benefit provided under the contract or negotiated by any other union and the Times in connection with the current extension negotiations Or at any time through March 39, 1993. Should the Union exercise this right, The Times Will pay, within Sixty (60) days of the date of termination, the Earnings Bonus due on 9rOSS wages for any prior bonus period.

name: Earnings Bonus 8. Benefit Calculation as if Wages Increased
text: 8. It is agreed that go long as this Earnings Bonus agreement applies, any benefit provided te employees by The Times pursuant to the Contract or otherwise which is calculated on or determined by the employee'¢ wage rate shall be calculated or determined as if the wage scales were increased by $25.93 per week. This provision Shall include by example, but not limitation, Times retirement or pension benefits, wick Pay and stock purchase options. Where a benefit such as Workers! Compensation, State Disability benefits or Unemployment Insurance requires a statement of wage rate, The Times will report the employee's wage rate as increased by $25.93 per week. This Paragraph shall be applied so as to eliminate any duplication of the Earnings benefit or wage rate. Further, nothing herein shall be construed to require The Times to make contributions to the FUNDO0001092 am ©} so Publishers '=NMDU Welfare Fund or NMDU-Publishers' Pension Fund on Earnings Bonus payments or to calculate such contributions as if the employee's wage scale were increased by $25.93 per week.
